[!WARNING]

Material for MkDocs is approaching end of life

Material for MkDocs is scheduled to reach end of life on November 5, 2026. Until then, maintenance is limited to critical bug fixes and security updates. After this date, the project will remain available on PyPI and GitHub, but no further maintenance is planned except in exceptional circumstances.

For users looking for a long-term, actively developed successor, we're building Zensical – a next-generation static site generator designed for technical documentation. If you're planning a new documentation project or evaluating your long-term options, we invite you to take a look.

Organizations requiring support beyond this date are welcome to get in touch to discuss available options.

Read the full announcement on our blog

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Hand the hero relaunch off from the checkpoint it was paused at (#8890)

The launcher still pointed at `step-54000`, which predates the
2026-09-03 pause. The hero was cancelled at step 58014 to free eleven
racks for the #8870 debugging window, and relaunching from `step-54000`
would silently discard the ~4,000 steps trained since — about a day of
training on 704 GPUs.

`step-58014` was forced through the training-control endpoint
immediately before the cancel, so the pause itself cost about one step
rather than the up-to-an-hour gap a scheduled temporary checkpoint would
have left. It is verified complete: `manifest.json`, `manifest.ocdbt`
and `metadata.json` all present, `{"step": 58014, "timestamp":
"2026-09-03T23:13:13.777258", "is_temporary": true}`, with 28,098
objects totalling 5.36 TB under `d/`.

It is a temporary checkpoint, which restore treats identically to a
permanent one. Both kinds are written by the same call in the same
format; `is_temporary` is read only by the deletion policy, never by
restore, and `_scan_checkpoint_root` accepts any directory containing
`metadata.json`, sorting all roots by step descending. `metadata.json`
is written last and only after the global commit barrier, so a torn
checkpoint is invisible to discovery rather than loadable-but-wrong. A
permanent checkpoint could not be used instead: the newest is
`step-54000`, the next is `step-60000` (~11.5 h away), and a permanent
one cannot be forced — `request_checkpoint()` sets only `should_save`,
while `save_permanent_ckpt` follows `force`, which is true only on clean
training completion.

The run id keeps its existing form and moves to the step it now forks
from: `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k`.

Note for #8833: the gate/router weight-decay run now starts from 58014
rather than 54000, so its control is the paused hero's own trajectory
rather than the step-54000 one.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
[grug] Default gate/router weight decay on in the hero recipe (#8833)

Decay the attn_gate and MoE router weights in the EP hero recipe, on by
default in the scaling ladder. Details:
https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8818

The decay peaks at 0.02, anneals linearly to 0 over `num_train_steps`,
and reads its coefficient from the Adam step `count`, so on a resume it
evaluates at the restored global step (≈0.017 at step 54k of the hero's
390,251, reaching 0 at the end). It is folded into `scale_by_adam`
without adding state, so the optimizer state stays
`optax.ScaleByAdamState`: a checkpoint trained without decay resumes
unchanged — Adam moments and step count preserved — and the decay
switches on from the resumed step. `--gate-router-weight-decay 0` leaves
the update byte-for-byte identical, so opting out reproduces the prior
behavior exactly. Only attn_gate and the router weight are decayed;
router_bias, embeddings, and the norm gains are untouched.

The continuation runs under its own run id rather than by relaunching
the hero, following the `--initialize-from-checkpoint` convention from
#8868. `trigger_hero.sh` starts `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step54k`,
forking `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` from its step-54000 checkpoint into a
fresh run and tree so the decayed run has a clean W&B history and the
source run is untouched. The hero recipe uses the pooled-wave transport
(`fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`, remat `recompute_all`) that the
step-54000 checkpoint was trained with, not the ragged all-to-all EP
path.

---------

Co-authored-by: Matt Wittmann <matt.wittmann@openathena.ai>

[grug] Fall back to the pooled-wave transport for the EP hero (#8884)

The d6144 EP hero moves tokens with `fixed_pooled_wave_all_to_all`
again, at the 1.15 sender and receiver capacity factors over 3 waves
that the spec already carries. The ragged transport hung an 11-rack hero
on the step after a watch step, twice, and a one-rack restore does not
reproduce it (#8870).

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rl] Add the curriculum-RL sampling experiment (#8769)

Add `experiments/post_training/curriculum_rl`, a SkyRL GRPO experiment
measuring what dynamic sampling curricula buy at a fixed generated-token
budget (tracking issue #8765; the full write-up with charts lives on the
issue and the `assets/curriculum-rl-paper` branch).

`pool.py` builds the graded prompt pool as a cached ArtifactStep: a
ladder of nineteen bins graded 0-13 by measured difficulty, spanning
procedural reasoning-gym arithmetic, GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MATH by level,
NuminaMath tiers, AIME, Omni-MATH, TheoremQA, and HARDMath (Putnam-AXIOM
is absent; every HF mirror is gated). It pins dataset revisions, carries
both `reward_spec` and `reward_model` ground-truth columns (environments
read different keys), elicits per-bin answer-line formats for the rule
graders, and drops rows whose templated prompt exceeds the prompt-token
cap — an over-length prompt skips generation and a fully skipped GRPO
group fails the trainer's admission invariant. `launch.py` wires pool
build, model adoption, RL training with terminal HF export, and
Evalchemy evaluation as cached ArtifactSteps, with per-round scale
presets for Qwen3-0.6B and the Snowball 67B-A2B SFT MoE (at full scale,
8 H100 nodes per arm: 4 FSDP2 training nodes plus 4 expert-parallel vLLM
engine nodes, MuonH, and an 8192-token generation budget in round 5).
`report.py` is a click group covering W&B report charts, Evalchemy
record aggregation, pool composition stats, and retained-trajectory
statistics (truncation, think-token, and answer-line compliance rates).

The sampling policies themselves (stateful curriculum sampler, per-bin
decayed pass statistics with prior reversion, per-row evidence tracking,
DAPO-style informative-group redraws) were upstreamed to MarinSkyRL in
marin-community/MarinSkyRL#470 and are already covered by main's pin.
`remote()` and the step runner gain a `pip_packages` passthrough to
fray's `create_environment` so the pool build can pin `reasoning-gym` at
the use site (matching skyrl-gym's version) without a marin extra.

Across five rounds (results and caveats on #8765): grade-seeded prior
sampling with DAPO redraws beat naive shuffling on grade-weighted score
at equal token budgets for both Qwen3-0.6B and Snowball (round 4: 0.292
vs 0.285; round 3: 0.310 vs 0.289), with the largest gains on
frontier-grade attainment; pure learnability-seeking samplers without a
grade prior starved easy bins and collapsed.

Part of #8765
